judged_text: In the reschedule path, when the reference's credentialId matches no calendarCredential in this.calendarCredentials and the prisma.credential.findUnique returns null, the local variable credential stays undefined and updateEvent(credential, event, ...) is still called with undefined. updateEvent(undefined, ...) dereferences credential.id / getCalendar(undefined) and throws a TypeError (prisma 'Malformed ObjectID' or getCalendar crash), so a reschedule of a booking whose referenced credential was deleted or belongs to a different user crashes instead of returning the graceful failure result the catch block promises — the booking update request fails with a 500.

adjudication.rationale: In EventManager’s reschedule/update path, the diff changes `calendarReference` to an array and loops over references. In the branch `if (reference.credentialId)`, it sets `credential = this.calendarCredentials.filter(...)[0];` and, if missing, tries `prisma.credential.findUnique(...)`. However, after that, it unconditionally does `result.push(updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId));` even when `credential` is still undefined (e.g., credential not in `this.calendarCredentials` and DB lookup returns null / lacks `app.slug`). This matches the finding: `updateEvent` will be invoked with an undefined credential and can crash when it dereferences credential/getCalendar.
